parts.text: A student uses a pendulum to determine a value for the acceleration of free fall g . Figs. 1.1 and 1.2 show the apparatus. Fig. 1.1 Fig. 1.2

ms.label: 1(b)
ms.text:
Either suitable use of a horizontal straight edge, explained briefly
Or holding rule close to pendulum
Or line of sight perpendicular (to rule)

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student displaces the pendulum bob slightly and releases it so that it swings. He measures the time t for 20 complete oscillations of the pendulum. 27.8 s t = ...............................................................

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Calculate the period T of the pendulum. The period is the time for one complete oscillation. T = ...........................................................[1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Measuring the time for a large number of oscillations, rather than for one oscillation, gives a more accurate value for T . Suggest one practical reason why measuring the time for 200 oscillations, rather than 20 oscillations, may not be suitable. ........................................................................................................................................... .......................................................................................................................................[1]

ms.label: 1(c)(ii)
ms.text: Pendulum may stop OR student may lose count

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Calculate the acceleration of free fall g using the equation g = 4 π 2 l T 2 . Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. g = ................................................. m / s 2 [2]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) The student checks the value of the acceleration of free fall g in a text book. The value in the book is 9.8 m / s 2 .

ms.label: 1(d)(i)
ms.text:
Explanation of cause of inaccuracy in measurement of t or l.
e.g. student did not react quickly enough when starting/stopping stopwatch OR difficulty in
measuring accurately to centre of bob

ms.label: 1(d)(ii)
ms.text:
Any two from:
Use different length(s)
Repeat timing
Use of a fiducial mark
Increased number of oscillations
2
Plot a graph using length and time or time
